A1.situation: At a bakery, you want two small cakes. What do you say?
A new neighbour says hello to you. What do you say?
You need a bus ticket. What do you say to the driver?
You cannot see the board. What do you tell your teacher?
It is your friend's birthday today. What do you say to him?
In a shop, you want to find the shoes. What do you ask?
Your cousin comes to your home. What do you say?
You want a table for two people. What do you ask the waiter?
Your brother shows you his new bike. What do you say?
You want to borrow two books from the library. What do you ask?
It is raining and Tom has no coat. What do you tell him?
You like your friend's new dress. What do you say to her?
A woman asks you the way to the bank. What do you say?
Your mother cooks a nice dinner. What do you say to her?
On a bus, you want the empty seat. What do you ask?
Your aunt sends you a postcard. What do you say to her?
You play football with friends and your team wins. What do you say?
At the hotel desk, you need your room key. What do you say?
A shop has nice apples. You want three. What do you say?
Your phone rings. It is your grandmother. What do you say?
You like a red hat in a shop. What do you ask?
Your sister helps you with your homework. What do you say?
You plan a picnic on Sunday. What do you ask your sister?
You are full, but your host offers more cake. What do you tell her?
Your new boss shakes your hand on your first day. What do you say?
The classroom is hot. What do you ask your teacher?
A tourist asks you to take her photo. What do you say?
You have two cinema tickets. What do you ask your friend?
At the post office, you need one stamp. What do you say?
You see your teacher in the supermarket. What do you say to her?
Your classmate sings very well in the school concert. What do you tell her?
Your neighbour has a nice garden. What do you say to him?
A waiter brings you soup, but you want salad. What do you say?
You want to pay by card in a shop. What do you ask?
Your little sister wants to play, but you are busy. What do you say?
At the zoo, you cannot find the lions. What do you ask a worker?
A boy at a party asks where you live. What do you say?
At the sports centre, you want to play tennis. What do you ask?
Your friend comes back from a holiday. What do you ask her?
On the phone, you cannot hear your cousin well. What do you ask him?

A2.situation: Your train is late and you will arrive after dinner. What do you tell your host?
You want to join a cooking class at the community centre. What do you ask at reception?
Last weekend, Sam helped you move house. What do you say to thank him?
Your taxi is twenty minutes late. What do you say when you phone the company?
A new student looks lost on her first day. What do you say to her?
You plan to visit the museum on Sunday. What do you ask when you phone?
Your neighbour asks you to water her plants next week. What do you say to her?
You left your scarf on a bus this morning. What do you ask at the station?
At the hairdresser, you want your hair a little shorter. What do you say?
Maria cooked dinner for you last night. What do you tell her when you meet today?
Your internet stopped working this morning. What do you say when you call the company?
You need a present for your dad's birthday. What do you ask the shop assistant?
Your colleague is going to a new job next week. What do you say to him?
You plan to cycle around the lake all day. What do you ask at the bike rental?
Your flatmate wants to go running tomorrow at six in the morning. What do you tell him?
Someone is sitting in your seat at the cinema. What do you say to him?
Because of rain, the match is now on Sunday. What do you tell your team?
Your pizza still has not come after an hour. What do you say when you phone?
Your English teacher gave you a good mark. What do you say to her after class?
You want to send a parcel abroad. What do you ask at the post office?
At the market, you think the cheese is too expensive. What do you say to the seller?
Your friend will visit your town next month. What places do you tell her about?
You missed yesterday's class because you were away. What do you ask a classmate?
Your neighbour's cat is in your kitchen again. What do you say to your neighbour?
You want to stay one more night at the hotel. What do you say at reception?
Your manager asks you to work on Saturday, but you have plans. What do you say?
Your colleague has two concert tickets for Friday and asks you to come. What do you reply?
You cannot find the milk in a large supermarket. What do you ask an assistant?
Your grandparents called to say they will visit on Saturday. What do you say?
You need someone to feed your fish next week. What do you ask your friend?
Your bus went past your stop without stopping. What do you tell the driver?
You want to learn the guitar, and your friend plays well. What do you ask him?
The bill at the restaurant has a dessert you did not order. What do you say?
You forgot to bring back the book Anna lent you. What do you tell her?
A visitor asks you about a good place to eat. What do you tell him?
You are going to be late for a meeting. What do you tell your colleague?
A friend wants to join your swimming club. What do you tell her about it?
You took the wrong coat home from a party. What do you say to its owner?
Your cousin did not reply to your messages all week. What do you ask him?
The library book you borrowed is late. What do you say to the librarian?

B1.situation: The air conditioning in your hotel room has stopped working. What do you tell reception?
Your colleague has offered to help with a report, but you have nearly finished it. What do you say?
Your language lessons feel too easy for you. What do you suggest to your teacher?
A colleague wants to borrow your car this weekend, but you need it yourself. What do you tell her?
You need to move your city tour from Tuesday to Friday. What do you tell the agency?
You can't figure out the office printer on your first day. What do you ask a colleague?
Your neighbours are organising a street party and ask for your help. What do you say?
You're offered a weekend course, but you've already made plans. What do you say to the organiser?
A customer asks you about a product you know little about. What do you say to her?
Your sofa delivery has been moved twice without notice. What do you say when you call the company?
Your friend has invited you to go hiking, but the forecast says heavy rain. What do you suggest?
You want to swap shifts with a colleague so you can attend a wedding. What do you ask?
Your study group always meets late in the evening, which doesn't suit you. What do you suggest?
A tourist asks which station is closest to the old town. What do you tell him?
Your gym's new opening hours mean you can't train before work. What do you tell the manager?
During your presentation, someone asks a question you cannot answer. What do you say to them?
Your landlord wants to visit the flat tomorrow, but you won't be home. What do you tell him?
You lent your brother some money a month ago, and he hasn't mentioned it. What do you say?
You booked a table for four, but six people are now coming. What do you tell the restaurant?
A colleague asks you to check her report today, but you are very busy. What do you say?
Your tutor wants you to lead the group project, but you feel unprepared. What do you say?
The jacket you like is only available in a larger size. What do you ask the assistant?
Your neighbour's tree has grown over your fence and blocks the light. What do you say to him?
A friend asks you to recommend a good book for her holiday. What do you suggest?
In a new city, you need a weekly travel pass. What do you ask at the ticket office?
You're looking after a new employee this week. What do you say to her on her first morning?
Your friend's dinner party clashes with a work event you must attend. What do you tell your friend?
You bought concert tickets for the wrong date. What do you ask the ticket office?
Not enough colleagues have signed up for the office football match. What do you say to the team?
The wifi in the cafe keeps cutting out while you are working. What do you ask the staff?
You need the library laptop for one more day before returning it. What do you ask the librarian?
Your neighbour collected your post while you were away. What do you say to her when you return?
You are interested in volunteering at a local animal shelter. What do you ask when you phone them?
You need next Friday off to move house. What do you ask your manager?
Your flatmate has just passed her driving test after three tries. What do you say to her?
Nobody at the bank has called your number after half an hour. What do you ask the staff?
A visitor's host is running twenty minutes late. What do you tell the visitor in reception?
Your sister wants to quit her course halfway through the year. What do you say to her?
The till charges more than the shelf price shows. What do you tell the cashier?
Your new phone's screen stopped responding after a week. What do you say at the shop?

B2.situation: You're asked to present results tomorrow, although the figures haven't been confirmed yet. What do you tell your manager?
A client wants a discount that your company policy doesn't allow. What do you say to her?
At a residents' meeting, higher building fees are proposed that you consider unjustified. What do you say?
Your colleague's proposal would double your team's workload if it were adopted. What do you say to him?
Your card has been charged twice for one hotel stay. What do you say when you call?
A promotion requiring relocation abroad is offered to you, but you need time. What do you tell your director?
A local reporter asks what you think of turning the old market into a park. What do you say?
Your department is being made to adopt software you've found unreliable. What do you say to the IT manager?
Your tenant has paid the rent late three months in a row. What do you say to him?
A colleague asks you to support her application for a role you also want. What do you say?
A university admissions officer asks why you chose to change subjects. What do you say?
Your neighbour suggests sharing the cost of repairing the fence between your gardens. What do you say?
A supplier has offered to deliver earlier if you pay a higher fee. What do you say?
You were charged a late fee because a call centre advised you wrongly. What do you say?
Your volunteer group is losing members, and you've been asked for ideas. What do you suggest at the meeting?
A colleague from another department keeps sending you tasks that aren't your responsibility. What do you say to her?
The coach wants extra training sessions, but many players can't attend them. What do you tell him?
A local gallery asks whether your photographs could be shown in its spring exhibition. What do you reply?
An interviewer asks how you would handle a disagreement with a manager. What do you say?
Your flatmate rarely contributes to cleaning, and it's starting to affect your friendship. What do you say to him?
Your company is considering a four-day week, and you've been asked for feedback. What do you say?
A customer insists on a refund for a product that was clearly used. What do you say to him?
Your course tutor has given you feedback that you consider unfair. What do you say when you meet her?
The renovation of your kitchen has been delayed by three weeks. What do you say to the builder?
A friend invites you to invest in her new bakery, but the risks worry you. What do you say?
Your manager is away, so you must chair this morning's meeting. What do you say to open it?
A conference organiser asks if you'd be willing to speak on a panel next month. What do you reply?
You'd never have joined the gym had you known about the hidden charges. What do you tell the manager?
Your library is reducing its opening hours, and users have been invited to comment. What do you say?
A neighbour wants to cut down a tree that you believe makes the street more pleasant. What do you say?
You've been invited to join a car-sharing scheme at work, but your hours vary. What do you say?
A travel agent offers a package that's cheaper but includes two long stopovers. What do you say?
A client has requested changes after the design was approved. What do you say to her?
Your elderly neighbour asks you to help her set up video calls with her family. What do you say?
An online seller has refused to accept your return, claiming the item was damaged by you. What do you say?
A colleague suggests moving weekly meetings to Friday afternoons, which you think is unwise. What do you say?
Your choir has been invited to perform abroad, but the cost is high for members. What do you suggest?
The school has asked parents for ideas on reducing waste in the canteen. What do you suggest?
A recruiter asks why there's a gap of a year in your work history. What do you say?
A new colleague is struggling to fit in with the team. What do you say to her?

C1.situation: A research partner has published preliminary findings without consulting you, despite your earlier agreement. What do you say to her?
You're stepping in as interim team leader during a colleague's extended leave. What do you tell the team?
A long-standing customer insists that a verbal promise made by your predecessor be honoured. What do you say to him?
Your neighbourhood association wants to ban weekend parties in the shared courtyard, which you consider heavy-handed. What do you say?
A reviewer has dismissed your paper's methodology without explanation. What do you say when you speak to the editor?
Rumours of a takeover are unsettling your staff, though nothing has been decided. What do you say at the briefing?
A colleague's presentation contained a factual error that the client has not yet noticed. What do you say to your colleague afterwards?
You are asked to justify why your department needs a larger share of next year's training budget. What do you say?
A prospective tenant asks whether the flat is quiet, though the bar downstairs can be lively. What do you say?
An interviewer presses you on why you left your previous role after only eight months. What do you say?
Your co-author wants to submit the manuscript before you are satisfied with the analysis. What do you say?
A festival committee has invited you to judge a photography competition in which a friend is entered. What do you say?
A client is reluctant to commit to a long-term contract given the current uncertainty. What do you say to reassure her?
Your manager's ambitious timeline seems unrealistic, but she is visibly committed to it. What do you say to her?
A hotel has overbooked and offers you a room at a sister property further away. What do you say?
You are asked to give the opening remarks at a colleague's retirement celebration. What do you say?
Two members of your book club regularly dominate the discussion, leaving others little chance to speak. What do you say?
A contractor claims unforeseen complications justify a substantial increase on the agreed price. What do you say to him?
A student challenges the fairness of an assessment criterion in front of the whole seminar group. What do you say?
Your proposal for flexible working has been met with polite scepticism from senior staff. What do you say to win them over?
A collaborator abroad repeatedly misses calls scheduled across time zones. What do you say when you finally speak?
An orchestra you volunteer for wants to raise ticket prices, which you fear will alienate loyal audiences. What do you say?
You discover that a supplier has quietly substituted a cheaper material without informing you. What do you say to them?
A mentee asks for candid advice about whether to pursue a doctorate or enter industry. What do you say?
The club committee wants to prioritise its competitive teams over beginners' sessions. What do you argue at the meeting?
A potential investor asks you to explain why your start-up's growth has recently plateaued. What do you say?
Your landlord proposes a rent increase well above the local average, citing recent renovations. What do you say?
A colleague confides that she is thinking of resigning and asks you not to tell anyone. What do you say to her?
You've been asked to give a visiting delegation an informal overview of your department's work. What do you say?
A neighbour's planned extension would block the afternoon sun from your terrace. How do you raise your concerns with him?
A translation agency has delivered work riddled with inconsistencies, just before your deadline. What do you say to them?
A journalist interviewing you about your research oversimplifies your conclusions. What do you say to correct him?
You have to tell a long-term volunteer that their role is being taken over by paid staff. What do you say?
A former classmate asks for your honest view of the novel she has spent five years writing. What do you tell her?
A museum curator asks for your view on whether interactive displays dumb down serious history. What do you say?
Your university wants to replace in-person seminars with recorded lectures, and student representatives are consulted. What do you say?
A loyal client asks you to bend the rules on a deadline that other clients must meet. What do you say?
A colleague suggests cutting corners on testing to meet a launch date. What do you say?
You have been invited to mediate between two neighbours arguing over a shared driveway. What do you say to open the conversation?
An event venue has cancelled your booking two weeks before the conference. What do you say when you call them?

C2.situation: A distinguished colleague's keynote rested on data you know to be outdated, and he asks for your candid impression. What do you say?
A benefactor offers a generous donation to your gallery on condition that she approves the exhibitions it funds. What do you say?
Your editor wants to soften a chapter's conclusions to avoid offending a powerful reviewer, which you find intellectually untenable. What do you say?
A protege's ambitious grant application is eloquent but, in your view, methodologically fragile. She asks you for frank feedback. What do you say?
A co-founder proposes pivoting to a lucrative market that sits uneasily with the company's founding ethos. What do you say?
The committee you chair has reached an impasse, with both factions entrenched and the deadline looming. What do you say to break the deadlock?
An admired author asks you to endorse a book whose central argument you find superficially persuasive but flawed. What do you say?
You are asked, at a panel discussion, to reconcile two apparently contradictory findings from your own published research. What do you say?
A client presses for an unequivocal guarantee on an outcome that is inherently uncertain. What do you say to him?
A rival firm's chief engineer approaches you informally about a possible collaboration, aware that your boards distrust each other. What do you say?
Your orchestra's new conductor favours radical reinterpretations that the regular audience finds alienating. As board chair, what do you say to him?
Your commissioned translator defends her liberal rendering of a poem as truer to its spirit. What do you say to her?
A doctoral candidate's thesis is brilliant in places yet marred by unsupported generalisations, and the viva is tomorrow. What do you say to him?
An architect proposes a striking design that would, however, compromise the building's accessibility. What do you say at the review?
A long-serving trustee resists every attempt at modernisation, invoking the founder's supposed wishes. What do you say to her privately?
A curator asks whether an artwork of contested authorship should be exhibited with a qualified attribution. What do you advise?
Your publisher wants to market your carefully nuanced study as a sensational exposure of scandal to boost sales. What do you say?
A seasoned negotiator on the other side makes a concession that seems suspiciously generous. What do you say in response?
An eminent historian at a symposium dismisses oral testimony as inherently unreliable, and the chair invites your response. What do you say?
Your team's elegant solution has been superseded by a cruder but cheaper alternative favoured by procurement. What do you say?
You must deliver an impartial appraisal of a programme designed by your closest ally on the board. What do you say to her beforehand?
A donor wants her name on the new library wing, which some staff consider ostentatious. As director, what do you tell them?
A sceptical client suspects your recommendation is self-serving because your firm would profit from it. What do you say?
Your research assistant has unearthed evidence that undermines the thesis of your forthcoming book. What do you say to her?
At a formal dinner, a guest confidently repeats an anecdote you know to be apocryphal. What do you say to him?
A colleague's reticence in meetings is being misread by management as indifference. What do you say to your director?
A festival director invites you to curate a programme but insists on retaining the final veto. What do you say?
Your mentor's latest proposal seems to repackage ideas he once dismissed as naive. He asks your opinion. What do you say?
An auditor's report, though technically accurate, conveys an impression of negligence you consider unwarranted. What do you say to the auditor?
A gifted but abrasive engineer alienates colleagues, yet the project depends on her expertise. What do you say to her?
A bidder at an auction you run disputes the hammer price, alleging ambiguity in your call. What do you say?
The editorial board wants to retract an article on grounds you regard as procedurally dubious. What do you say?
A tenant association's spokesperson accuses your firm of neglecting maintenance, and some of the accusations are well founded. What do you say?
A visiting scholar critiques your department's curriculum as parochial, and colleagues look to you to respond. What do you say?
A heritage body objects to your company's restoration plans as insufficiently faithful to the original. What do you say?
Your business partner wants to accept an offer you regard as undervaluing years of painstaking work. What do you say?
An acclaimed chef asks your verdict on a tasting menu that is technically dazzling but emotionally cold. What do you say?
You must persuade a cautious funding panel that a speculative line of inquiry merits support. What do you say?
A former student, now a rival, credits you only obliquely in an influential paper. What do you say when you meet?
Your dissertation supervisor suggests framing modest findings as a breakthrough to attract attention. What do you say to her?
